head: claude/claudebot-answerable
title: feat(telegram): make the Claude bot polled, then move decision prompts to it
body:
## Summary

Operator, 2026-09-02: *"that's supposed to be showing up in Cloudbot. Right? Not on the trader one, the decisions."*

Work-decision prompts move from the trader bot to the dedicated Claude bot (`@ict_cluade_bot`) — **and the thing that makes that safe ships in the same PR**: a new service polls `TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET` and registers the `wdec` callback handler, so the bot is *answerable* before anything is routed to it.

**Tier-2** — a live service gains a polling loop and a new unit is added. No order path, no strategy config, no risk caps.

## Why this is two halves and not a route change

PR #10778 (`133587f1`) shipped the round-trip onto the **trader** bot deliberately, and its reasoning is preserved rather than overturned:

> **Delivery and answerability are different properties.** A `sendMessage` needs only a token. An inline-keyboard **button is inert** unless some process is POLLING that bot and has a `CallbackQueryHandler` registered — the tap emits a `callback_query` that nobody collects.

Re-verified by reading the code on this clone at `133587f1`, not taken on trust:

| token | polled by | callback handler |
|---|---|---|
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` (trader) | `ict-telegram-bot.service` | yes — `CallbackQueryHandler(callback_handler)` |
| prop token (via `_prop_route()`) | `ict-claude-bridge.service`, despite the name | yes — `CallbackQueryHandler(on_callback)` |
| **`TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET`** | **nothing** | **n/a** |

`telegram_query_bot.main()` already constructs a `Bot(token=claude_route().token)` — but only to **send** pings. It never polls it. That is the gap in one file.

So re-pointing `answerable_route()` alone would have shipped **dead buttons that look healthy** — strictly worse than the wrong chat, because a wrong channel is visible and an unreceived tap is not.

## The architecture decision, and why — a second `Application` vs a new unit

Both were considered. **A new unit won**, on three grounds:

1. **`run_polling()` does not compose.** It builds and *owns* an event loop, installs signal handlers, and blocks. Two of them in one process means hand-rolling `initialize()` / `start()` / `updater.start_polling()` for both and driving shutdown yourself — i.e. rewriting the lifecycle of the process that owns the operator's **kill switch** and account-mode UI, for a feature unrelated to either. The Prime Directive makes that trade badly.
2. **One process is one event loop.** A stall in the decision channel would become a stall in the kill switch. `Restart=always` per unit also means a crash-looping decision bot cannot take the trader UI down with it.
3. **Separately readable journal** (`journalctl -u ict-claude-decision-bot`) — the same reasoning already written into `ict-claude-bridge.service`, whose delivery failures were invisible while its logs went to a repo-path file.

**The cost, stated rather than buried:** a new unit must be installed and enabled on the VM. `scripts/install_systemd_units.sh` does this (idempotent, gateway VM excluded), but it only happens on the next deploy run. The cheaper option would have avoided that; it was not worth the blast radius.

## Making the dead-button state reportable

The `position_idx`-shaped hazard here is that a token resolving while nothing polls it produces a prompt that **arrives, renders, and highlights on tap** while doing nothing. New `src/runtime/telegram_poll_registry.py` makes that a state somebody can read — **three, never collapsed**:

- `polled_with_handler` — a live process claims it polls this token **and** handles this prefix.
- `token_only_not_polled` — we **looked**; a tap would not be received.
- `unknown` — we could **not** look. Fails closed, but stays a distinct value.

Collapsing `unknown` into the first ships dead buttons; collapsing it into the second condemns a working channel on the strength of an unreadable file and silently reroutes every decision. **The two errors are opposite**, which is why the third value exists rather than being inferred from a boolean.

**Evidence, not declaration.** The claim is a *heartbeat* a live poller refreshes, so a process that dies, hangs or is stopped has its claim expire on its own. `TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_POLLED=1` would have been one line and a lie the moment the unit was masked — *a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard*.

**Registered with `collapsed-state-guard`** as `telegram_poll.poll_state` — 3 consumers, all states read, guard clean. Its `consumer_token` is scoped to the **reading** vocabulary rather than the module name: `telegram_query_bot.py` imports the module to *record* a claim and never reads a state back, and a module-name token matched it and then found the word `"unknown"` in an unrelated heartbeat label. That is the coincidental-English false positive the guard's own header warns about; the honest fix is a precise token, not an override annotating a file as "legitimately sees only one state" when it sees none.

One deliberate union, stated in the module rather than hidden: *nothing polls this* and *something polls it but not for this prefix* share `token_only_not_polled`, because they are one decision — a tap is not received either way — and the sub-condition survives in `note`. What must never merge is *we looked* with *we did not*.

## It degrades rather than going silent

With the Claude bot unconfirmed, prompts fall back to the **trader** bot — the wrong chat, **loudly and countably**: `destination` + `poll_state` in the sweep stats, a WARNING naming a **state-specific remedy** (start the service vs check the registry — different faults, different fixes), and a startup banner per bot naming which token it polls and which prefixes it handles.

That direction is a judgement call, so it is flagged rather than assumed: **a wrong chat is a noise complaint; holding every decision prompt is an outage.** It matches the posture already written into `telegram_query_bot.py` for Claude pings — *"Separation is a nice-to-have; delivery is not."* Only when **neither** bot is confirmed polled does the sweep hold, counted as `held_not_polled` and never pooled with `held_route` (no destination at all). **If the reviewer prefers fail-closed, that is a one-line change and I will make it — but I will not make it silently.**

## Architecture impact

- [ ] **Not applicable**
- [x] **Architecture docs updated** — `docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md` gains the service-topology row and a Change-log row. It qualifies on two counts: a new deployment unit and a new inter-process contract.

## Test plan

- [x] The **73 existing** tests in `tests/test_telegram_decisions.py` still pass, unmodified.
- [x] **111** in the two decision/registry modules (73 + 38 new): the routing change, the not-polled hold, all three states emitted and read, `unknown` failing closed, a heartbeat expiring a dead claim, `held_not_polled` never pooled with `held_route`, and no token **value** in any note, banner or persisted entry.
- [x] A test asserts the `/api/diag/log_file` paths match what `entry_path()` actually writes — a read surface pointing at the wrong path answers "absent" forever, which this vocabulary would render as `token_only_not_polled`: a **working** poller reported as a dead button.
- [x] **Full suite: 14,512 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed.** The one failure on the first run (`test_deploy_service_set_matches_canonical`) was mine and is fixed — a new unit owes the canonical set, `deployment-ops.md`, and a same-PR record.
- [x] **All 52 relevant guards pass** on the *committed* tree (the runner is explicit that an uncommitted diff scans nothing).
- [x] `ruff check .` clean at the repo's pinned `>=0.15,<0.16`.
- [ ] CI green

### A green harness cannot prove this

**The done-condition is a real tap on ClaudeBot producing a `work_decision_transit.jsonl` row** — the manager's to run with the operator.

Every passing test above is **equally true of a process that is never started**. The failure this change exists to prevent has no external symptom, so green CI is precisely the evidence that cannot settle it. Worse, the fallback makes the failure *quiet-but-working*: **"decisions still arrive" is not evidence the move happened.** Read `destination` in the sweep stats, or `/api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude` — never the mere arrival of a prompt.

Tracked as `OI-20260902-DECISION-PROMPTS-MOVED-TO-CLAUDEBOT-AND-NO-TAP-HAS-LANDED-THERE` (`loud: true`), which spells out that merging does not clear it, a green run does not clear it, and *the bot being polled* does not clear it either — that is necessary and is not the same as a tap being received and submitted.

### Two honesty notes

- **Not verified by me:** I am told the round trip is already proven on the **trader** bot as of `2026-09-02T10:16:36Z` (`chosen: accept_ungated`, `submitted_by: telegram`). `runtime_logs/` is gitignored, so the transit log is unreachable from a session clone and **I did not confirm it**. This PR changes *where* it happens, not *whether* it works.
- **`TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET` on the VM is not something I can read.** If it is absent, that is an operator/manager action — reported, not worked around, and **not** substituted with `TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN`, which drives the **prop** bot despite its name. Without it the unit exits `EX_CONFIG` (78) and `RestartPreventExitStatus=78` stops it in a visible `failed` state rather than crash-looping a log line every 15s — restarting cannot set an env var.

The repo is public: `TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET` is referenced **by name only**, and a test asserts no token value reaches a note, banner, log line or persisted entry.

## Filed for follow-ups

- `callback_handler`'s `wdec` branch still tests the **literal** `"wdec"` while the encoder and the poll claim both use `CB_PREFIX`. A rename would move two of the three and leave the dispatcher behind. Noted in-place rather than fixed, because a concurrent session (`claude/claude-ping-double-delivery-x4mq2p`) has declared that file — see the collision note below.
- `unwired-artifact-guard` gained a **fourth** reference shape, `python -m <dotted.module>`. `deploy/**/*.service` has always been in `RUNNER_GLOBS`, so the corpus was right and only the pattern was blind: a systemd `ExecStart` carries a dotted module path, which can never contain `.py` and is not an `import`. It graded `src/bot/claude_decision_bot.py` "no runner references it at all" while its own unit runs it. Annotating `# wiring: manual-only` would have been the cheap fix and a **false statement**. Negative control **run, not assumed**: with a genuinely unwired file planted and committed, the guard still reported it.

## Concurrent-session collision

`claude/claude-ping-double-delivery-x4mq2p` declared `src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py`, and #10778's own DONE comment flagged it as *"the one most likely to touch the same regions."* My edit there is deliberately **small and additive** — a poll registration plus one log line, immediately before `run_polling()` — with the substantive work in new modules. Board `START` posted on #6927 ([comment](https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/issues/6927#issuecomment-5508095033), via the `board-post` relay: `add_issue_comment` 403s from this session).

**Draft, and not to be merged by me.**
